;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Operation Barkhane]]
***The office of [[President of France|French President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] says that a [[French Armed Forces|French soldier]] was killed during operations against militants in [[Mali]]. According to the press release, the soldier died when his [[armored vehicle]] was hit by an [[improvised explosive device|IED]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-sahel-security-france/french-soldier-killed-in-mali-combat-operations-elysee-idUSKCN24O2LR?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]; [[July 2020 Afghanistan attacks]]
**The [[Taliban]] attacked the [[Maruf District]], [[Kandahar Province|Kandahar]], [[Afghanistan]], killing two [[Afghan National Police|policemen]] and wounding twelve others. The assault was repulsed, resulting in 27 Taliban fighters being killed. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-07/24/c_139237464.htm (Xinhua)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
**The [[Cabinet Office (Japan)|Cabinet Office of Japan]] plans to declare that [[Economy of Japan|its economy]] has entered a [[recession]] after 71 months of growth. [http://www.asahi.com/ajw/articles/13571531 (''Asahi Shimbun'')]
*[[Germany|German]] [[universal bank]] [[Degussa Bank]] is put up for sale as [[parent company]] [[M. M. Warburg & Co.|M. M. Warburg]] raises funds to pay off fines and debts incurred from its participation in Germany's biggest post-war fraud scheme. The Bank is valued between [[Euro|€]]200-400 million. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-degussa-bank-sale/germanys-degussa-bank-put-up-for-sale-sources-idUKKCN24O2D2?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Tokyo]] reports its highest one-day increase in COVID-19 cases, with 366 new cases reported. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-07-23/tokyo-finds-more-than-300-virus-cases-thursday-most-ever-nhk (Bloomberg)]
****[[Japan]] reports its record number of new COVID-19 cases for two consecutive day, with 980 new cases reported. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2020/07/ea25950c58b2-breaking-news-tokyo-reports-over-300-new-daily-virus-infections-record-figure.html (Kyodo News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Hong Kong]] reports 118 new [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases, a new record in two consecutive days. The new cases include 111 cases that were locally transmitted. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/healthcoronavirus-hongkong/hong-kong-reports-new-daily-record-of-coronavirus-cases-idUKL5N2ET1QP (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] reports a record of 45,720 new COVID-19 cases, taking its total number of cases to 1.24 million. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-india/india-reports-record-45720-new-coronavirus-cases-deaths-rise-by-1129-idUSKCN24O0E3 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iraq]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on aviation]]
****[[Baghdad International Airport]] reopens for commercial flights after months of closure during the COVID-19 pandemic. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1708901/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****The [[United States]] surpasses four million cases of COVID-19. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2020/07/23/united-states-coronavirus-cases-deaths-timeline/5485674002/ (''USA Today'')]

;International relations
*[[Afghan peace process]]
**The [[United States]] condemns Wednesday's [[airstrike]]s against the [[Taliban]] in [[Herat Province|Herat]] which resulted in 45 deaths, many of them civilians. The U.S. special envoy [[Zalmay Khalilzad]] said that children were killed and also condemned recent Taliban attacks. The Afghan government defends the airstrikes as an operation against the group. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-airstrike/u-s-envoy-condemns-afghan-airstrikes-against-taliban-as-civilians-among-45-killed-idUSKCN24N2PZ (Reuters)]
*[[China–United Kingdom relations]]
**[[China]] says the [[United Kingdom|UK]] is violating international law by allowing a path to British citizenship for Hong Kong residents with a [[British National (Overseas) passport|BNO passport]], and threatens to stop recognising the BNO. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-china-hongkong/china-threatens-to-stop-recognising-bno-passports-of-hong-kong-residents-idUKKCN24O009?feedType=mktg&feedName=topNews&WT.mc_id=Partner-Google (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[Killing of George Floyd]]
**[[George Floyd protests]]
***[[George Floyd protests in Portland, Oregon]]
****[[Portland, Oregon|Portland]] Mayor [[Ted Wheeler]] is tear-gassed in the city's downtown, according to video from a ''[[The New York Times|New York Times]]'' journalist. The video shows Wheeler, wearing goggles and a face mask amid a crowd of people, holding his nose and closing his eyes in distress as a cloud of tear gas drifts by him. It is unknown at this time who is responsible for deploying the tear gas and there is nothing to indicate the mayor was targeted. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/23/us/portland-protests-mayor/index.html (CNN)]
****[[United States Department of Justice Office of the Inspector General|Inspector General]] [[Michael E. Horowitz]] announces that there will be an investigation into the [[United States Department of Justice|Justice Department]]’s use of force against protesters. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/justice-department-inspector-general-investigation-portland-federal-law-enforcement/ (CBS News)]
**[[Police reform in the United States]]
***[[Governor of Minnesota|Minnesota Governor]] [[Tim Walz]] signs a law banning various forms of chokeholds. [http://www.hastingstribune.com/news/national/minnesota-gov-walz-signs-police-accountability-bill-sparked-by-george-floyds-death/article_ebf80f91-87cb-502f-a417-c3d5b3028a5e.html (''The Hastings Tribune'')]
*[[2019 Samoa assassination plot]]
**The Supreme Court of [[Samoa]] denies a bid by two of the three defendants in the case to be able to return to [[Australia]], where they have permanent residencies. The Court argued that, aside of the lockdown due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], "no amount of surety bond would overcome the risk of the men not returning for their trial", which is set for November. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/421805/samoa-assassination-plot-accused-denied-australian-return (RNZ)]
*[[LGBT rights in Israel]]
**Israeli MPs pass a bill to begin the process to outlaw [[conversion therapy]], being the first Middle Eastern country to do so. The bill was passed as two of the main coalition parties joined the opposition in supporting it. It must pass two more approvals to become a new law. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-53511329 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]]
***[[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]] announces that the [[2020 Republican National Convention]] in [[Jacksonville, Florida|Jacksonville]] will be cancelled. [https://www.npr.org/2020/07/23/894874198/president-trump-cancels-jacksonville-portion-of-republican-national-convention (NPR)]
**[[2020 Bolivian general election]]
***The general election is postponed until October 18 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia|COVID-19 pandemic in the country]], which has infected more than 64,000 people, and killed more than 2,300. This is the second time the Interim Government has delayed the elections since the [[2019 Bolivian political crisis]] late last year that forced the resignation of former president [[Evo Morales]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bolivia-politics-election/bolivia-election-delayed-to-oct-18-as-pandemic-grips-nation-idUSKCN24O2PY?il=0 (Reuters)]
*The 91-year-old [[Emir of Kuwait|Emir]] of [[Kuwait]] [[Sabah Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah]] flies to the United States to seek further medical treatment after undergoing successful surgery days ago. [https://apnews.com/b44925da8af1738518125830eee04eff (AP)]

;Science and technology
*[[Censorship in Malaysia]]
**[[Ministry of Communications and Multimedia (Malaysia)|Malaysian Communications Minister]] [[Saifuddin Abdullah]] retracts his announcement yesterday that video producers on social media would require a license per the 1981 [[National Film Development Corporation of Malaysia]] (FINAS) Act, following public outcry. The initial proposal was made following [[Government of Malaysia|the government]]'s dispute with [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]] over a documentary concerning the discrimination migrant workers faced in the country [[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia|during the COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/politics/article/3094418/malaysia-you-now-need-licence-tiktok-or-facebook-videos (''South China Morning Post'')] 
*[[Militarisation of space]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] and [[United States]] accuse [[Russia]] of conducting an [[anti-satellite weapon]] test in space. Russia's [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Ministry of Defence]] says it was testing new technology on Russian space equipment. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-53518238 (BBC News)]
*The [[China National Space Administration]] successfully launches [[Tianwen-1]], China's first independent [[interplanetary mission]] to [[Mars]], from [[Wenchang Spacecraft Launch Site]] in [[Wenchang]], [[Hainan]]. The mission includes an [[orbiter]], lander and [[Mars rover|rover]], which will search for evidence of both current and past life on the planet. [https://www.nbcnews.com/science/space/china-launches-ambitious-attempt-land-rover-mars-rcna59 (NBC News)]

;Sports
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**[[2020 Major League Baseball season]]
***[[Major League Baseball]] begins its season after a four-month delay caused by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/29435596/2020-mlb-season-glance-opening-day-schedule-previews-picks-more (ESPN)]
*[[National Hockey League]]
**The [[Seattle]] [[expansion team]] set to begin play in the 2021–22 season announces its name of [[Seattle Kraken]]. [https://www.nhl.com/news/seattle-kraken-nickname-for-nhl-expansion-team/c-317588092 (NHL)]
*[[Washington Redskins name controversy]]
**The [[Washington Redskins]] change their name to the Washington Football Team for the rest of 2020. The new name is a placeholder, and a permanent name will be announced in the future. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2020/07/23/washington-redskins-new-team-name-washington-football-team/ (''The Washington Post'')]
